question: Can learning to reconstruct a random portion of each training row teach a useful Task1 representation beyond a randomly initialised encoder? Compare matched downstream heads, then let the existing development election decide whether to use or blend them.
relationship: Inspired by the masked-value reconstruction principle in Yoon et al., VIME, NeurIPS 2020. The experiment uses explicit mask tokens and column-specific categorical reconstruction on the fitting partition.
data: 4,061 bound fitting rows only for ordinal vocabularies, removal of constant or partition-identical fields, neural pretraining and supervised heads. Unknown categories get a separate token in each field. Held features enter only prediction. No test, designated validation, external pretrained weights, or model API.
architecture: Per-field 12-dimensional embeddings, 128 hidden channels and 24 shared output components. For 40 epochs mask 30% of field values and minimize cross entropy on hidden cells, without labels. Same initialized encoder and heads for both sides. Frozen representations augment the existing contextual tree with 24 numeric columns; separately fine-tune each encoder for 24 supervised epochs with identical minibatch and dropout seeds. One self-supervised optimizer fit, two tree fits and two supervised neural fits. Save trained weights privately for reuse.
decision: Freeze all four prediction matrices first. Using 808 nomination rows, select retain or one of four heads at shares 0.125,0.25,0.5,1 against the established research pair. On 817 and 807 later rows require nonnegative on each and at least .003 pooled before a larger blind study. If attributing a gain to pretraining, apply the nominated head's same weight to its scratch counterpart and require nonnegative paired gain on each check and a strictly positive sum. Report direct head-to-head regardless of nomination.
